transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-08-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Park (SearchSpark Head of Search), Aaron Cho (SearchSpark ML Eng), Priya Singh (SearchSpark CTO)

00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm Maya, AE on the accounts team, with Diego and Sofia from solutions engineering. how's everyone doing?
00:08 Lena Park: good, thanks. excited to see the embeddings and rerank flow, we currently use Elastic for our vector search but relevance isn't great for long queries.
00:18 Diego Ramos: awesome, we'll do a 30-minute walkthrough and then leave time for Q&A. quick question on scope: are you focused on first-stage retrieval or candidate reranking?
00:27 Aaron Cho: both — we do BM25 for first pass and then embeddings-based rerank, but our rerank is slow and inconsistent. target is <100ms added latency for top-10.
00:40 Sofia Patel: got it. i'll demo a hosted flow: embeddings endpoint -> FAISS/Pinecone-like store -> Redwood rerank endpoint (we call a /rerank endpoint in the demo) that re-scores candidates with cross-encoder style prompt.
00:54 Maya Chen: also to flag -- we support dedicated capacity and private VPC installs if you need stricter isolation, but today we'll focus on hosted API.
01:05 Aaron Cho: for compliance, we need SOC2 + SSO and we use AWS KMS. any issues with that?
01:12 Diego Ramos: no, hosted supports encryption at rest and in transit, we integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments; for hosted we have customer-side key management notes in the security pack. we'll share SOC2 artifacts and SAML+SCIM docs after the call.
01:25 Priya Singh: ideal for us is to avoid moving PII out of customers region — any data residency options?
01:30 Maya Chen: we have region routing for hosted and Private/VPC options if you need on-prem or specific region controls.
01:37 Sofia Patel: ok jumping into demo. i have a small notebook. step one: obtain embedding from /v1/embeddings. here's a sample request using model "redwood-embed-v1" — note this is our curated open model, you can also bring your own.
01:52 Diego Ramos: small note on model choice: dense embeddings vs sparse — if you have long product descriptions, embedding dimension and truncation matter. we usually recommend 1536d for semantic similarity.
02:06 Aaron Cho: we use 1024 dims today. will switching blow up cost?
02:10 Sofia Patel: there's a cost delta per vector, but the quality improvements are often worth it. our Optimize tool can recommend quantization (8-bit or 4-bit) and batching settings to hit cost targets.
02:22 Lena Park: how do you do rerank? is it a separate cross-encoder?
02:26 Sofia Patel: yes, rerank is a second-stage request. flow: first-stage embed + vector index to fetch top-K candidates, then call /v1/rerank with the query and candidates. the rerank model cross-attends to all candidates so it is heavier but you only run on top-K (usually 10-50).
02:42 Diego Ramos: example latency numbers: on hosted we typically see 20-40ms per embedding call, and rerank depends on number of candidates; rerank 10 candidates on a medium model is ~60-120ms. for your SLO ~100ms we might recommend a smaller rerank model or aggressive batching/quantization.
03:02 Aaron Cho: that's in line with our concerns. Are there streaming responses for rerank?
03:06 Sofia Patel: rerank returns scores — no streaming. for generation we stream, but rerank is a synchronous score response.
03:14 Lena Park: indexing — we currently use Elastic vectors plugin. can we keep that and call Redwood for embeddings and rerank?
03:20 Diego Ramos: yes, many customers do that. Redwood embeddings can be stored in Elastic or Pinecone; we also have a managed vector store option if you want us to host indexes.
03:29 Priya Singh: cost comparison with Pinecone?
03:32 Maya Chen: Pinecone is competitor for vector storage; we position Redwood to handle both the embeddings + the rerank compute so it's fewer moving parts. cost varies by throughput and model sizes; we'll include a pricing sheet.
03:44 Aaron Cho: curious about cache — we get a lot of repeated queries.
03:48 Diego Ramos: we support prefix KV cache and shard-level reuse. for rerank specifically you can cache candidate embeddings or rerank outputs for TTL windows. our runtime will also do continuous batching to improve GPU utilization.
04:01 Lena Park: what about evaluation? can we run A/B tests?
04:05 Sofia Patel: yes, Console supports rollouts and canarying across models, you can route a percent of traffic to a new reranker and compare metrics. Optimize can surface quality regressions tied to your eval set.
04:17 Priya Singh: security again — if we go hosted, where are logs stored, and do you support audit logs and idp SAML?
04:24 Diego Ramos: audit logs retained per account, access controlled via RBAC and SSO. we'll share the retention options; for enterprise we offer longer retention and an audit log export.
04:36 Maya Chen: quick demo of a rerank request — i send a POST to /v1/rerank with query and array of candidate passages; response has scores and explanations (if you enable structured output).
04:48 Sofia Patel: side note on explanation: it's model-assisted tokens, not deterministic provenance; it's useful for debugging but not a full provenance system.
04:58 Aaron Cho: great. two practical things: 1) can we test with our dataset (1M docs), 2) can you run a benchmark with our latency SLO?
05:08 Maya Chen: yes, we can set up POC. typical approach: we provision a small dedicated pool or use hosted with guaranteed shards for the run, run the script that fetches top-100 from your index and reranks top-10, and measure p99/p50 latency and cost per query.
05:24 Lena Park: what's the onboarding time for POC?
05:27 Maya Chen: we can start within a week once we have dataset sampling and an NDA if needed; POC usually 2 weeks.
05:33 Priya Singh: are there any gotchas with API rate limits during POC?
05:36 Diego Ramos: we'll set temporary higher limits and guidance on batching. also note tokenization differences between models can affect per-token costs.
05:46 Aaron Cho: what about model updates and version pinning?
05:49 Sofia Patel: Console lets you pin model versions and rollout gradually. also our runtime can fallback to cheaper variants if a model is unavailable; that's useful for reliability.
06:00 Lena Park: do you support customer-managed keys for hosted?
06:03 Diego Ramos: for hosted we don't have per-tenant KMS today — Private supports full customer KMS/HSM integration. for hosted, we provide encryption and strict controls; we can discuss hybrid options in the contract.
06:18 Maya Chen: ok wrapping up, summary of action items and next steps. we'll send the pricing deck and SOC2 by Tuesday, Diego will upload the demo notebook and rerank examples, and we propose a 2-week POC starting next week pending dataset exchange.
06:34 Lena Park: sounds good — Aaron will share a 100k sample to start and we'll coordinate about credentials.
06:40 Priya Singh: thanks, please include dedicated capacity numbers in the pricing, we may prefer that for consistent latency.
06:45 Maya Chen: absolutely. thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with next steps.

Notes on transcription: occasional crosstalk, product names transcribed as "redwood-embed-v1" but sometimes as "redwood embed one". Occasional words like "K V cache" instead of KV cache.

End of meeting.
